title: Field-induced incommensurate--commensurate transitions in anisotropic magnets
authors: P. T. Bolokhova, A. V. Syromyatnikov
abstract: We study field-induced incommensurate--commensurate transitions (ICTs) in classical spin chains with Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI) $D$, strong easy-plane anisotropy, and weak easy-axis anisotropy $A$ within the easy plane. This model describes systems with ferromagnetic layers coupled by exchange interaction with DMI. The magnetic field $\bf H$ is applied in the easy plane at an arbitrary angle $δ$ to the easy axis stabilizing a soliton lattice in the ground state. We consider ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic in-chain exchange interactions within the continuum limit and show that the easy-axis anisotropy leads to qualitatively different effects in these two cases: the ferromagnetic chain is described by a double-sine-Gordon-type equation with phase-shifted harmonics, whereas the antiferromagnetic chain reduces to a sine-Gordon equation. For the latter case, phase boundaries between incommensurate and commensurate states are found analytically in $(H,A,D,δ)$ space and confirmed by numerical calculations for certain $D$ and $δ$ values. Close to all ICTs, results of the continuum consideration become invalid due to a stochastic destruction of near-separatrix solutions which either make an ICT a first-order transition or stabilize states with spatially irregular soliton and antisoliton arrangements.
summary: This theoretical work examines how external magnetic fields drive phase transitions between ordered (commensurate) and quasi-periodic (incommensurate) magnetic states in anisotropic spin chains. By deriving continuum equations for both ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic couplings, the authors map out the phase boundaries. Crucially, they highlight that while continuum theory is useful, real-world lattice effects cause the incommensurate state to become unstable right at the transition point.
main_problem: The paper investigates field-induced incommensurate-to-commensurate transitions (ICTs) in anisotropic magnetic spin chains.
main_result: The continuum theory successfully predicts phase boundaries for the antiferromagnetic case, but near the transition, discreteness effects cause the incommensurate state to become unstable, suggesting first-order transitions.
method: The study employs the continuum limit approximation to solve the discrete spin chain model, deriving effective sine-Gordon-type equations for both ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic chains.
model_or_system: The model consists of classical spin chains featuring Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction (DMI), strong easy-plane anisotropy, and weak easy-axis anisotropy. The system is analyzed for both ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic exchange interactions.
key_observables: Incommensurability parameter (inverse period of the soliton lattice), phase boundaries between commensurate and incommensurate states, and the effective magnetic field $h_{	ext{eff}}$.
important_parameters: DMI ($D$), easy-axis anisotropy ($A$), applied magnetic field ($H$), and the angle ($\delta$) between $H$ and the easy axis. The analysis assumes these are small compared to the exchange coupling $|J|$.
main_assumptions: The primary assumption is the use of the continuum limit approximation, which is explicitly noted to break down near the ICTs due to lattice pinning effects.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematic spin configurations, phase diagrams mapping commensurate vs. incommensurate regions, and the dependence of the incommensulability parameter on the magnetic field, comparing analytical predictions to numerical results.
paper_structure: The paper analyzes the system separately for ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic chains, deriving distinct continuum equations (double-sine-Gordon vs. sine-Gordon). It then uses these equations to find analytical phase boundaries, confirming them with numerical simulations while discussing the breakdown of the continuum theory near critical points.
why_interesting: The study of soliton dynamics and phase transitions in low-dimensional magnetic systems is highly relevant to understanding emergent quantum phenomena in condensed matter, particularly in systems exhibiting strong spin-orbit coupling effects.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic spin configurations in the xz plane of antiferromagnetic chain (1). (a) Typical incommensurate arrangement. (b) Typical commensurate (spin-flop) arrangement for a misaligned easy axis a and the field h (the angle between the field and the easy axis δ = 3π/10 for definiteness). (c) Commensurate (spin-flop) configuration at δ = 0 and h2 > 8a. (d) Commensurate (antiferromagnetic) configuration at δ = 0 and h2 < 8a.

FIG. 2. Phase diagrams of the antiferromagnetic chain obtained analytically in the continuum approximation from Eq. (14) and confirmed numerically for different angles δ between the magnetic field h and the easy axis. Here α = 0.01 defines the DMI value (see Eq. (3)). Pink and violet regions correspond to commensurate and incommensurate phases, respectively. Typical spin arrangements in these phases are shown in Fig. 1.

FIG. 3. Incommensurability parameter ζ (the inverse period of the soliton lattice) as a function of the magnetic field h. Points show numerical findings obtained from finite-difference solutions and the dashed line represents the analytical solution in the continuum approximation. Very close to the ICT, the incommensurate phase becomes unstable against a spatially irregular soliton state so that ζ cannot be smaller than a critical value shown by the horizontal dashed line (see the text).

Solitons.note: The investigation of field-induced incommensurate-to-commensurate transitions and the derivation of effective sine-Gordon-type equations directly relates to the physics of commensurate-incommensurate transitions and soliton lattice stability.
